en: I take refuge in the six-faced one, whose limbs are anointed with sandalwood paste, who possesses a broad chest, whose divine vehicle is a peacock, the son of Rudra, the lord of the world of the gods, the deity who is kind to Brahmanas. ||1||

I take refuge in the God who is devoted to Brahman—the one who blazes with splendor, who is worshipped by the hosts of gods, who dwells in the temple on the banks of the Dhārā river, O Kumāra, who possesses the form of Kandarpa and limbs of exquisite beauty. ||2||
I take refuge in the God who is devoted to Brahman, the incarnation of Śeṣa, whose form is lovely, who possesses twelve divine eyes and twelve arms, and who bears the trident and the sword. (3)

I take refuge in Kumāra, the best of gods, the friend of Brahman, who shines in the terrible battle with the enemy of the gods, who wields the spear, and whose hands are adorned with the weapon of the sharp-edged *śakti*. (4)

O Brahmin, I take refuge in the son of Īśa, who bestows the accomplishment of desired goals; the giver of sweet food; the wish-fulfilling cow; the source of the Gaṅgā; the one who is favorable to all people; and the God who is devoted to the Brahmins. ||5||

Whoever here recites these five verses with devotion, having fixed their mind upon the God who is the Friend of Brahman, shall obtain every enjoyment desired on earth, and at the end, they joyfully attain identity with Guha.
